title: K-Beauty and Biopharmaceuticals Drive 19.4% Surge in South Korea's Biohealth Exports; Annual $30 Billion Milestone in Sight for First Time - BigGo Finance
text:

 Add preferred source South Korea's cumulative biohealth industry exports for the first three quarters of this year reached $24.75 billion, up 19.4% from the same period a year earlier and a record high. Cosmetics led growth at $11.13 billion, up 31.0%, while pharmaceuticals rose 14.2% to $8.93 billion and medical devices gained 6.2% to $4.7 billion. Biopharmaceuticals grew 17.0% on strong European demand, but exports to the US fell 30.0%. The Korea Health Industry Development Institute projects that annual exports could surpass $30 billion for the first time ever if demand holds through the rest of the year, while flagging expanded US tariffs and European regulatory overhaul as variables. Key Elements 
 Korea Health Industry Development Institute Choi Young-im biohealth industry cosmetics exports biopharmaceuticals CDMO biosimilar botulinum toxin medical devices US pharmaceutical tariffs South Korea's biohealth industry exports reached $24.75 billion (approximately 32.7 trillion won) through the first three quarters of this year, setting a new all-time high for the period. Cosmetics and pharmaceuticals both posted double-digit growth rates, lifting overall results, and projections suggest annual exports could exceed $30 billion (approximately 39.7 trillion won) for the first time ever if the trend continues.
 According to the "2026 Q3 Cumulative Biohealth Industry Export Performance" report released on the 27th by the Korea Health Industry Development Institute, cumulative exports rose 19.4% from $20.73 billion (approximately 27.4 trillion won) in the same period last year. The institute expects European demand for biopharmaceuticals and Western demand for basic skincare products to continue through the remainder of the year, anticipating a breach of the $30 billion annual mark.
 By category, cosmetics showed the most pronounced growth. Cosmetics exports rose 31.0% to $11.13 billion (approximately 14.7 trillion won), marking the highest cumulative third-quarter performance on record. Basic skincare products, which account for 78.3% of total cosmetics exports, drove growth with a 37.7% increase to $8.71 billion (approximately 11.5 trillion won). By country, exports to the US rose 49.1% to $1.8 billion (approximately 2.4 trillion won), while the UK surged 210.5% to $400 million (approximately 530 billion won), the Netherlands jumped 366.1% to $330 million (approximately 440 billion won), and Canada soared 155.1% to $250 million (approximately 330 billion won). Body cleansing products also rose 30.6% to $550 million (approximately 730 billion won), setting a record for cumulative third-quarter performance.
 Pharmaceutical exports increased 14.2% to $8.93 billion (approximately 11.8 trillion won). Among these, biopharmaceuticals grew 17.0% to $5.71 billion (approximately 7.6 trillion won), accounting for 64.0% of total pharmaceutical exports. Growth in the European market was particularly notable, with exports to Switzerland up 23.9%, Hungary up 27.9%, the Netherlands up 43.1%, and Belgium up 208.5%. The expansion is attributed to increased contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) supply of biopharmaceuticals and rising demand for biosimilars. However, biopharmaceutical exports to the US fell 30.0% to $890 million (approximately 1.2 trillion won) over the same period, presenting a contrast.
 Exports of toxins and toxoids, including botulinum toxin, rose 43.1% to $430 million (approximately 570 billion won), setting a record high. Exports to the US increased 94.9%, while China, Brazil, and Vietnam grew 19.2%, 30.6%, and 55.0%, respectively.
 Medical device exports rose 6.2% to $4.7 billion (approximately 6.2 trillion won). Ultrasound imaging diagnostic devices increased 10.7% to $750 million (approximately 990 billion won), setting a record high, while medical laser equipment rose 15.2% to $420 million (approximately 560 billion won). In contrast, in-vitro diagnostic device exports fell 2.4% to $520 million (approximately 690 billion won).

 Looking at detailed growth rates by major export category, basic skincare products form the backbone within cosmetics, while biopharmaceuticals anchor pharmaceuticals. In particular, biopharmaceuticals showed even growth across European countries but declined in the US, revealing regional disparities.
 Choi Young-im, Director of the Biohealth Innovation Planning Division at the institute, assessed that "cumulative biohealth industry exports in Q3 2026 saw both pharmaceuticals and cosmetics set new record highs, while medical devices continue their steady increase with each passing quarter." She added, "European demand for biopharmaceuticals and Western demand for basic skincare products appear likely to continue through the remainder of the year," and "annual biohealth industry exports are expected to surpass $30 billion for the first time ever this year."
 However, regulatory changes in major markets are cited as variables. Director Choi emphasized, "US pharmaceutical tariffs are gradually expanding depending on product category, and Europe is pursuing pharmaceutical system reforms and mandatory medical device registration—the regulatory environment in major markets is changing rapidly, making agile monitoring of policy changes by country and proactive response more important than anything."
 This performance demonstrates that South Korea's biohealth industry export structure is being reorganized around two pillars: cosmetics and biopharmaceuticals. Cosmetics continue high growth driven by US and European demand for basic products, while pharmaceuticals depend on Europe-centered CDMO and biosimilar demand. Some observers suggest that if US pharmaceutical tariff expansion and European regulatory reforms take full effect, regional performance disparities could widen further. Whether annual exports surpass $30 billion will depend on fourth-quarter European biopharmaceutical demand and Western cosmetics consumption trends.
